# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 20 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 20 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_020_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 20

**20:1** Joseph was just getting ready to move on through Judea when the whole of Bethlehem erupted in commotion. A group of Magi had arrived from the east, going around asking: "Where is the child who was born to be king of the Jews? We saw his star rise in the east and we've come to bow down before him."

**20:2** Word reached Herod and he was shaken. He dispatched his officers to intercept the Magi and called in the chief priests for a private interrogation in his palace. "What do the scriptures say about where the Messiah is to be born?" They answered without hesitation: "Bethlehem of Judea. That's what the text says." Herod sent them away.

**20:3** He then turned to the Magi. "Tell me exactly what you saw — what was the sign of this king's birth?" The Magi described it: "There was a star — enormous, blazing — outshining everything else in the sky. The other stars faded in its light. We took it as a sign that a king had been born in Israel. That's why we're here."

**20:4** "Go," Herod said smoothly. "Search carefully. When you find him, come back and tell me, so I can go and pay my respects too."

**20:5** The Magi set off, and there was the star again — moving ahead of them, guiding them all the way to the cave, where it stopped and hovered directly overhead. Inside they found the baby with his mother Mary. They reached into their traveling packs and brought out their gifts: gold, frankincense, myrrh.

**20:6** Then God warned them in a dream not to go back through Herod's territory. They found another road home.
